info.description:
Cyberbank Core is a banking service for financial institutions to perform fundamental banking functions:

- Create and maintain bank accounts such as DDAs, checking accounts, and savings accounts
- Manage account features such as overdraft coverage and protection
- Manage interest accrual and payment
- Create transactions such as deposits, withdrawals, and money movement
- Create and manage holds and pending transactions

post.description: Use the Create Account endpoint to create an account for an existing customer. You must provide a customer ID for this endpoint.

Use the Close Account endpoint to close an account. You must provide an account ID for this endpoint. ## Error codes This endpoint may return the following error codes: | HTTP status | Description | | :----: | ----- | | 400 | **`BAD_REQUEST`** — The request was not acceptable, typically due to missing or invalid parameters. | | 404 | **`NOT_FOUND`** — The requested entity does not exist. | | 422 | **`ACCOUNT_IN_EOD_PROCESSING`** — The account is in end-of-day processing and cannot be closed; retry after end-of-day processing completes | | 422 | **`ACCOUNT_NOT_OPEN`** — The account is not in an open status and cannot be closed | | 422 | **`ACTIVE_HOLDS_EXIST`** — Active holds exist for the account and must be released before it can be closed | | 422 | **`OUTSTANDING_PENDING_TRANSACTIONS_EXIST`** — Unresolved pending transactions exist for the account and must be resolved before it can be closed | | 422 | **`UNRELEASED_FUNDS_AVAILABILITY_EXISTS`** — The account has funds not yet released by its funds-availability schedule; those funds must be released before it can be closed | | 422 | **`ACCOUNT_HAS_NEXT_DAY_TRANSACTIONS`** — The account has future-dated transactions and cannot be closed | | 422 | **`CLOSE_ACCOUNT_WITHOUT_INTEREST_ACCRUAL_PREVIOUS_DAY`** — The account does not have an interest accrual record for the previous business day and cannot be closed | | 422 | **`CLOSEOUT_DIRECTION_MISMATCH`** — The direction of the supplied transaction code does not match the computed closeout direction | **This endpoint may also return common error codes**.

Use the Preview Close Account endpoint to calculate the closeout amount an account would settle to on closure, using the same rules as a real closure, without mutating anything. Account status, balances, ledger, and accrued interest are unchanged; no transaction is posted and no closure event is emitted. The returned amount is a point-in-time estimate for the business date it was computed on—it is not a hold and does not reserve funds. If something posts to the account between this preview and a real closure, the real closeout amount can differ. It enforces every closure guard except those tied to posting the closeout transaction—the direction check on the supplied transaction code is validated only when the real close is performed—so the caller learns of a blocking account condition before attempting the close rather than after. The request body is the same shape as Close Account, so a caller can preview and then close with an identical payload. Fields that only exist to record the closeout transaction (`transactionSpecification`, `transactionCode`, `externalTransactionId`, `comments`, `description`, `serialNumber`, `clientMetadata`) are accepted for schema parity but are ignored here—this operation posts nothing, so they do not affect the computed amount. ## Error codes This endpoint may return the following error codes: | HTTP status | Description | | :----: | ----- | | 400 | **`BAD_REQUEST`** — The request was not acceptable, typically due to missing or invalid parameters. | | 404 | **`NOT_FOUND`** — The requested entity does not exist. | | 422 | **`ACCOUNT_IN_EOD_PROCESSING`** — The account is in end-of-day processing and cannot be closed; retry after end-of-day processing completes | | 422 | **`ACCOUNT_NOT_OPEN`** — The account is not in an open status and cannot be closed | | 422 | **`ACTIVE_HOLDS_EXIST`** — Active holds exist for the account and must be released before it can be closed | | 422 | **`OUTSTANDING_PENDING_TRANSACTIONS_EXIST`** — Unresolved pending transactions exist for the account and must be resolved before it can be closed | | 422 | **`UNRELEASED_FUNDS_AVAILABILITY_EXISTS`** — The account has funds not yet released by its funds-availability schedule; those funds must be released before it can be closed | | 422 | **`ACCOUNT_HAS_NEXT_DAY_TRANSACTIONS`** — The account has future-dated transactions and cannot be closed | | 422 | **`CLOSE_ACCOUNT_WITHOUT_INTEREST_ACCRUAL_PREVIOUS_DAY`** — The account does not have an interest accrual record for the previous business day and cannot be closed | **This endpoint may also return common error codes**.

Use the Create Pending Transaction endpoint to record a provisional ledger entry that contributes to the Pending Balance until it is resolved. The transaction is recorded against the current business date — `businessDate` and `effectiveDate` are not accepted on this endpoint.

The request is idempotent on the `X-GFT-Idempotency-Key` header; a replay using the same idempotency key returns `409 Conflict` with the body of the original successful response. A pending transaction whose creation would breach the available-balance sufficiency check (when enabled for the transaction code) is rejected with an `INSUFFICIENT_AVAILABLE_BALANCE` error. Backdated requests are rejected with a `PENDING_BACKDATING_NOT_ALLOWED` error. Reuse of an `externalTransactionId` already associated with another pending transaction is rejected with an `EXTERNAL_TRANSACTION_ID_ALREADY_USED` error. When a `fundsAvailabilitySchedule` is provided on a credit, the schedule is created atomically with the pending transaction; if the schedule cannot be created the pending transaction is not created either.

get.description: Use the List Pending Transactions endpoint to retrieve the pending transactions recorded against the specified account. Results may be filtered by lifecycle `status` (`PENDING` or `RESOLVED`). Results are paginated using opaque continuation tokens; pass the `nextPage` value from the previous response as the `page` parameter to retrieve the next page. ## Error codes This endpoint may return the following error codes: | HTTP status | Description | | :----: | ----- | | 400 | **`PAGE_TOKEN_INVALID`** — The provided page token is malformed and cannot be decoded | **This endpoint may also return common error codes**.

Use the Get Pending Transaction endpoint to retrieve the full `PendingTransaction` resource by its identifier. The response carries the request payload plus identifiers, lifecycle `status`, accounting `direction`, the recording `timestamp`, and `resultingBalances` reporting the balance dimensions captured at the latest lifecycle event applied to the entry. Once the transaction has been resolved (`status: RESOLVED`), the response additionally carries a `resolution` object with the resolution outcome, timestamp, and any posted-transaction identifiers booked when the entry was settled.

Set `idType` to indicate how the `{transactionId}` path value is interpreted:

- `transactionId` (default) — the value is an internal transaction identifier.
- `externalTransactionId` — the value is a caller-supplied external identifier; it is
  resolved within the specified account (external transaction IDs are unique only within
  an account).


Pending-transaction endpoints are served only while the deposits ledger runs using new  ledger structure; a request made in legacy ledger mode is rejected with `PENDING_NOT_SUPPORTED_IN_LEDGER_MODE` and the route behaves as if it were not registered (`404 Not Found`). When `idType` is `transactionId` (or omitted), a path value that is missing, blank, or does not conform to the required unsigned-positive-integer format is rejected with `INVALID_ARGUMENTS`. When `idType` is `externalTransactionId`, the path value must satisfy the external-transaction-id charset and length constraints enforced by the API schema. A request whose path `accountId` does not identify an existing account is rejected with `ENTITY_NOT_FOUND`. A request whose lookup identifier does not identify a pending transaction on the account is rejected with `PENDING_TRANSACTION_NOT_FOUND`; a pending transaction that belongs to a different account than `accountId` is reported identically and is therefore indistinguishable from one that does not exist.

post.description:
Use the Resolve Pending Transaction endpoint to settle or cancel a pending transaction. The mechanism is Matched Reversal: the pending entry is released atomically with any posted transaction(s) booked on a `SETTLE` resolution, succeeding or failing together.

Pass `resolution: SETTLE` together with up to ten `transactions` entries to book the posted transaction(s); the settle amount may differ from the pending amount and may be split across multiple posted entries (e.g., principal plus fee). Pass `resolution: CANCEL` with no `transactions` field to release the pending entry without settlement; any associated funds-availability schedule is removed and the held funds are released.

The request is idempotent on the `X-GFT-Idempotency-Key` header; a replay using the same idempotency key returns `409 Conflict` with the body of the original successful response. Resolving a pending transaction that has already been resolved (by a different request, not a replay) is rejected with `PENDING_TRANSACTION_ALREADY_RESOLVED`.

Use the Create Transaction Reversal endpoint to reverse a posted transaction on the current business day. This endpoint creates a compensating transaction with the same amount as the original and the transaction code associated with the reversal of the original transaction.

Use the Update Funds Availability Schedule endpoint to atomically cancel all currently active (unreleased) funds availability tranches on a previously posted credit deposit and replace them with a new set, or clear the schedule entirely via `unset` to release all held funds immediately. An auditable `reason` is required on every request for Regulation CC compliance. Exactly one of `fundsAvailabilitySchedule` or `unset` must be provided; supplying both is rejected with `FUNDS_AVAIL_UPDATE_SCHEDULE_UNSET_CONFLICT`, and supplying neither is rejected with `FUNDS_AVAIL_UPDATE_SCHEDULE_UNSET_MISSING`. The target transaction must already carry a funds availability schedule; attempting to add a schedule to a deposit posted without one is rejected with `FUNDS_AVAIL_UPDATE_NO_EXISTING_SCHEDULE`. All tranches in the new schedule must have an `availableFrom` strictly after the current UTC date-time; submitting a schedule where any tranche is past- or current-dated is rejected with `FUNDS_AVAIL_UPDATE_ANY_TRANCHE_EXPIRED`. To release funds on specific tranches immediately, omit them from the new schedule instead of back-dating them; to release everything held, use `unset`. An update that would change nothing is rejected with `FUNDS_AVAIL_UPDATE_NO_OP_REJECTED`: an `unset` on a transaction with no currently active tranche has nothing to release, so it is never reported as a success. Supplying replacement tranches on a transaction whose tranches were all already released or cancelled is not a no-op — it re-holds the funds and succeeds. The request is idempotent on the `X-GFT-Idempotency-Key` header; a replay under the same key returns `409 Conflict` with the body of the original successful response. Concurrent updates to the same schedule are serialized; a request that cannot acquire access within the wait threshold is rejected with `FUNDS_AVAIL_UPDATE_CONFLICT`. This endpoint is served only while the deposits ledger runs in new-ledger mode; a request in legacy or dual mode is rejected with `FUNDS_AVAIL_UPDATE_NOT_SUPPORTED_MODE`. ## Error codes This endpoint may return the following error codes: | HTTP status | Description | | :----: | ----- | | 400 | **`FUNDS_AVAIL_SCHEDULE_REQUIRES_CREDIT`** — The target transaction is not a credit; a funds availability schedule can only be updated on a posted credit deposit | | 400 | **`FUNDS_AVAIL_UPDATE_NO_EXISTING_SCHEDULE`** — The target transaction was posted without a funds availability schedule; adding a schedule to a deposit that has none is out of scope for this operation | | 400 | **`FUNDS_AVAIL_UPDATE_ANY_TRANCHE_EXPIRED`** — One or more tranches in the requested schedule has an availableFrom on or before the current UTC date-time; omit those tranches or use unset to release funds immediately | | 400 | **`FUNDS_AVAIL_UPDATE_INVALID_REASON`** — The supplied update reason is not one of the allowed FundsAvailabilityUpdateReason values | | 400 | **`FUNDS_AVAIL_SCHEDULE_EXCESS_INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`** — The requested schedule exceeds the original transaction amount or the available balance cannot cover the net increase in held funds | | 400 | **`FUNDS_AVAIL_SCHEDULE_CURRENCY_MISMATCH`** — A tranche currency does not match the currency of the deposit | | 400 | **`FUNDS_AVAIL_SCHEDULE_AVAILABLE_FROM_NOT_IN_FUTURE`** — A tranche availableFrom is on or before the current UTC date-time | | 400 | **`FUNDS_AVAIL_UPDATE_SCHEDULE_UNSET_CONFLICT`** — Both fundsAvailabilitySchedule and unset were provided; exactly one is required | | 400 | **`FUNDS_AVAIL_UPDATE_SCHEDULE_UNSET_MISSING`** — Neither fundsAvailabilitySchedule nor unset was provided; exactly one is required | | 404 | **`FUNDS_AVAIL_UPDATE_TRANSACTION_NOT_FOUND`** — The target transaction could not be found for the provided account | | 404 | **`FUNDS_AVAIL_UPDATE_NOT_SUPPORTED_MODE`** — Funds availability schedule updates are not supported because the account is not in new-ledger mode | | 409 | **`FUNDS_AVAIL_UPDATE_CONFLICT`** — The update could not acquire serialized access to the schedule within the wait threshold; retry shortly | | 422 | **`FUNDS_AVAIL_INVALID_TRANSACTION_STATUS`** — The target transaction is in a status that does not allow its funds availability schedule to be updated | | 422 | **`FUNDS_AVAIL_UPDATE_NO_OP_REJECTED`** — The update would not change the schedule; there is no active tranche to cancel and no replacement tranche was requested | **This endpoint may also return common error codes**.

200.description: The funds availability schedule was successfully updated.

post.description: Use the Update Account Hold endpoint to change the amount and/or expiration date of an existing hold. For further instructions and explanations, see Updating Holds. Identify the hold with `{holdId}`, interpreted as an internal `holdId` (default) or a caller-supplied `externalReferenceId` according to the `idType` query parameter. The operation is idempotent on the `X-GFT-Idempotency-Key` header, replay semantics: a replay using the same idempotency key returns `409 Conflict` with the body of the original successful response. ## Error codes This endpoint may return the following error codes: | HTTP status | Description | | :----: | ----- | | 400 | **`BAD_REQUEST`** — The request was not acceptable, typically due to missing or invalid parameters. | | 404 | **`NOT_FOUND`** — The requested entity does not exist. | | 422 | **`NO_OP_HOLD_UPDATE_REJECTED`** — The hold update would not change the hold amount or expiration; no-op updates are rejected | | 422 | **`HOLD_AMOUNT_WOULD_GO_NEGATIVE`** — The requested update would drive the hold amount below zero which is not allowed | | 422 | **`HOLD_UPDATE_CURRENCY_MISMATCH`** — The update amount currency does not match the currency of the account | | 422 | **`STALE_HOLD_UPDATE_REJECTED`** — The update's requestor timestamp is older than the recorded ordering anchor; out-of-sequence updates are rejected | | 409 | **`HOLD_ALREADY_RELEASED`** — The target hold has already been released or expired and cannot be updated | | 404 | **`ACCOUNT_HOLD_NOT_RELATED`** — The target hold does not belong to the specified account | | 422 | **`EXPIRATION_DATE_IN_THE_PAST`** — Hold expiration date cannot be before the current business date | **This endpoint may also return common error codes**.

Use the Resolve Account Hold endpoint to update the target hold's amount and/or expiration date while posting one or more transactions against the account, all committed atomically: the hold update and every transaction in `transactions` succeed or fail together. Identify the hold with `{holdId}`, interpreted as an internal `holdId` (default) or a caller-supplied `externalReferenceId`, according to the `idType` query parameter. The operation is idempotent on the `X-GFT-Idempotency-Key` header: a replay using the same idempotency key returns `409 Conflict` with the body of the original successful response and posts neither the hold update nor the transactions a second time. Because a hold is non-terminal — it stays `VALID` even when driven to a $0 amount — the idempotency key is the sole protection against double-posting on retry. There is no terminal hold state to short-circuit a replay, so `X-GFT-Idempotency-Key` is load-bearing here in a way it is not for pending resolution, where the pending transaction reaches a terminal resolved state. Always send the same key when retrying. ## Error codes This endpoint may return the following error codes: | HTTP status | Description | | :----: | ----- | | 400 | **`BAD_REQUEST`** — The request was not acceptable, typically due to missing or invalid parameters. | | 404 | **`NOT_FOUND`** — The requested entity does not exist. | | 422 | **`NO_OP_HOLD_UPDATE_REJECTED`** — The hold update would not change the hold amount or expiration; no-op updates are rejected | | 422 | **`HOLD_AMOUNT_WOULD_GO_NEGATIVE`** — The requested update would drive the hold amount below zero which is not allowed | | 422 | **`INSUFFICIENT_AVAILABLE_BALANCE`** — Insufficient available balance to book the requested transaction | | 422 | **`HOLD_UPDATE_CURRENCY_MISMATCH`** — The update amount currency does not match the currency of the account | | 422 | **`STALE_HOLD_UPDATE_REJECTED`** — The update's requestor timestamp is older than the recorded ordering anchor; out-of-sequence updates are rejected | | 400 | **`TRANSACTION_REASON_NOT_VALID`** — The provided transaction code and reason code pair is not compatible with this operation | | 404 | **`TRANSACTION_REASON_AND_REASON_CODE_DOESNT_EXIST`** — The provided transaction code and reason code pair is not defined in the system | | 409 | **`HOLD_ALREADY_RELEASED`** — The target hold has already been released or expired and cannot be updated | | 404 | **`ACCOUNT_HOLD_NOT_RELATED`** — The target hold does not belong to the specified account | | 422 | **`EXPIRATION_DATE_IN_THE_PAST`** — Hold expiration date cannot be before the current business date | **This endpoint may also return common error codes**.

200.description: The hold was updated and the transactions were posted.

post.description: **Deprecated.** This endpoint is being phased out. No removal date has been set yet — clients will be given a notice period before it is discontinued. This endpoint is deprecated because we want consumers to use Pending Transactions when funds should be available on a future date, not immediately. Holds should not be used for that purpose. Migration path depends on how you use it today: - If you combine `createHold`/`releaseHold` with `createTransaction` (including the At Work `releaseHold` + `createTransaction` pattern) to place a hold and later settle it, migrate to the Pending Transactions capability instead: Create Pending Transaction and Resolve Pending Transaction. Pass BTC/ETC in the `transactionCode` string field (example: `A2A_TRANSFER_PENDING.DB/SAME_MEMBER`). Do not send the old integer transaction code and reason code. - If you use the `createTransaction` action on its own for an immediate post, use Create Deposits Account Transaction directly. - If you use the `createHold` action on its own for a true hold — not to delay funds until a future date — use Create Account Hold directly. - If you use the `releaseHold` action on its own for a true hold, use Delete Account Hold with `?idType=holdId` or `?idType=externalReferenceId` directly. Use the Transact Account Actions endpoint to execute a sequence of actions against the specified account. With this endpoint you specify a sequence of actions that will execute without allowing other actions to intervene during the sequence. The actions are performed atomically, meaning that if one of the actions fails, all of the actions in the sequence are rolled back.

holdTypes.name: holdTypes
holdTypes.description:
Specify one or more hold types to be retrieved. Possible values:
- `CARD_ONLINE_AUTH` — Funds held for pending debit or credit card authorizations.
- `FUNDS_AVAILABILITY` — Funds held from deposits that have not yet cleared and are therefore unavailable for withdrawal.
- `COLLATERAL` — Funds held as collateral for a loan or held as a pledge for other purposes.
- `JUDICIAL_ORDER` — Funds held in response to a court order.
- `CUSTOMER_ORDER` — Funds held at the account holder's request.

FundsAvailability.title: Funds Availability
FundsAvailability.description:
Funds-availability information for a deposit transaction (`debitOrCredit: CREDIT`) that was created with the `fundsAvailabilitySchedule` object populated in the Create Transaction request.

For standard transactions without a funds-availability schedule, this object is not present.

fundsAvailable.description:
Amount of funds from this deposit that are available for withdrawal. This amount includes funds that were never part of a funds-availability schedule as well as scheduled amounts that have already been released: `creditAmount` minus `originalUncollectedTotal` plus `releasedToDate`.

This amount is <> because the value might be negative if the original total of scheduled tranches exceeded the deposit amount — for example, for cash-back deposits where the hold was larger than the deposited amount.

This amount is computed at the time this endpoint is called, so the value reflects which tranches have been released as of the moment of the request.

fundsUnavailable.description:
Total of unreleased amounts, meaning the total of tranches that have not reached their `availableFrom` time and are still unavailable for withdrawal.

This value is <> because individual tranche amounts are always positive — the aggregate cannot be negative. It can legitimately be `0.00` when all scheduled tranches have already been released (commonly seen with `scheduleTranchesStatus: PENDING`).

This value is computed at the time this endpoint is called, so the value reflects which amounts are released as of the moment of the request.

PendingTransactionStatus.title: Pending Transaction Status
PendingTransactionStatus.description: The lifecycle status of a pending transaction. While `PENDING`, the transaction contributes to the Pending Balance and the Available Balance reflects its impact. Once `RESOLVED`, its contribution is released; the resolution outcome (`POSTED` or `CANCELLED`) is reported separately on `resolution.outcome`. This enum is distinct from `TransactionStatus` (the posted-transaction P/S/X enum) and is not interchangeable with it.

AuthorizationRange.title: Authorization Range
AuthorizationRange.description: Optional partial-authorization range for a pending transaction. When supplied alongside the requested `amount` (the requested maximum), it declares the inclusive band within which the authorizing function may hold a partial amount. The actual approved value is reported back on the response `amount`. When `ranges` is present, both bounds are required; an incomplete range fails schema validation rather than silently defaulting.

partialMaxAmount.description: The maximum amount that may be approved for this pending transaction.

CanonicalTransactionCode.title: Canonical Transaction Code
CanonicalTransactionCode.description: The transaction code identifies the type of transaction and, via the transaction-code catalog, determines the accounting direction (DEBIT or CREDIT) and the set of account product types for which the transaction is permitted. Codes are dotted/slashed identifiers drawn from the platform catalog (e.g., `A2A_TRANSFER_PENDING.DB`), optionally qualified with an extended code after a `/`. See Transaction Codes for the full catalog.

authorizationRange.description: Optional partial-authorization range, additive to `amount` (the requested maximum). When omitted, the request shape is unchanged and the full `amount` is requested. When present, both `partialMinAmount` and `partialMaxAmount` are required.

When present, the schedule is created atomically with the pending transaction; if the schedule cannot be created, the pending transaction is not created. The schedule is released when the pending transaction is cancelled and is not carried over to the posted transaction(s) on settlement — the resolve request may declare a fresh schedule on each posted transaction.

ResolutionOutcome.title: Resolution Outcome
ResolutionOutcome.description: The outcome of resolving a pending transaction. `POSTED` indicates the resolution settled the pending entry by booking one or more posted transactions; `CANCELLED` indicates the pending entry was released without any settlement.

PendingTransactionResolution.title: Pending Transaction Resolution
PendingTransactionResolution.description:
Captures the resolution event for a pending transaction. Present on `PendingTransaction` only when `status` is `RESOLVED`.

Invariant on `postedTransactionIds`: when `outcome` is `POSTED` the array contains the identifiers of the posted transactions booked when this pending transaction was settled (one entry for a single-transaction settlement, additional entries for multi-transaction settlements); when `outcome` is `CANCELLED` the array is empty or absent. The polymorphism standard forbids `oneOf`/`anyOf`, so the outcome-conditional rule is enforced by the server rather than expressed declaratively in the schema.

resolvedAt.description: The exact time when the pending transaction was resolved. Format: RFC 3339 (ISO 8601) YYYY-MM-DD`T`hh:mm:ss.sss`Z`.

postedTransactionIds.description: Identifiers of the posted transactions booked when this pending transaction was settled. Non-empty when `outcome` is `POSTED`; empty or absent when `outcome` is `CANCELLED`.

supersededByTransactionId.description: Identifier of the successor pending transaction that replaced this one via a `:supersede` operation. Present only when `outcome` is `CANCELLED` as the result of a supersede; absent for a plain cancel or a `POSTED` settlement. Lets a reader trace the supersede chain from the superseded pending to its successor.

PendingTransaction.title: Pending Transaction
PendingTransaction.description:
A provisional ledger entry that contributes to the Pending Balance until it is resolved. A pending transaction is created by an originating business function (e.g., debit-card authorization, wire fraud screening) and may only be resolved by that same function. Resolution either settles the entry by booking one or more posted transactions (`resolution.outcome: POSTED`) or releases the entry without settlement (`resolution.outcome: CANCELLED`).

Note on `fundsAvailabilitySchedule`: this property inherits the request-side validation constraint `minItems: 1` from `CreatePendingTransactionInput`. When the original create request did not declare a schedule, the server omits this property from the response entirely; it is never returned as an empty array.

Note on `resultingBalances`: while `status: PENDING` the field reports the balance dimensions captured immediately after this pending entry was recorded; once `status: RESOLVED` it reports the balance dimensions captured immediately after the pending entry was resolved.

direction.description: Accounting direction (DEBIT or CREDIT) of this pending transaction, derived from the transaction code's catalog entry.

timestamp.description: The exact time when the pending transaction was recorded. Format: RFC 3339 (ISO 8601) YYYY-MM-DD`T`hh:mm:ss.sss`Z`.

productAndSubProduct.description: Deprecated: use `productCode` instead. This object will be removed in a future major release.

resolution.description: The resolution event for this pending transaction. Present only when `status` is `RESOLVED`.

PendingTransactionReference.description: Reference returned when a pending transaction is recorded. Carries the identifiers and balance impact a caller needs to continue without a follow-up read. Mirrors the `DepositsAccountTransactionReference` shape, with `pendingBalance` substituted for `ledgerBalance` because a pending entry moves the Pending Balance and the Available Balance, not the Ledger Balance.

amount.description: The actual approved value held for this pending transaction. On a partial approval this may be less than the requested `amount` from the request; full-vs-partial is derivable by comparing this value to the requested amount.

pendingBalance.description: The total amount of unresolved pending transactions reducing the Available Balance, captured immediately after this pending transaction was recorded.

fundsAvailabilitySchedule.description: Schedule tranches recorded with this pending entry. Present only when the request included a `fundsAvailabilitySchedule` array.

ResolvePendingTransactionInput.description: Input for resolving a pending transaction. The mechanism is Matched Reversal: the pending entry is released <<glossary:atomically>> with any posted transaction(s) booked on `SETTLE`, succeeding or failing together.

SettlePendingTransactionPostedTransactio.description:
One posted transaction to book on `@resolve SETTLE`. Core — not the caller — always determines the posted date; `businessDate`, `effectiveDate`, and `requestedDate` are not accepted.

Note on shape: this is a structural fork of `CreateDepositsAccountTransactionInput` with the date fields omitted. `CreateDepositsAccountTransactionInput` remains unchanged and is still used by `@supersede` and direct-posted transactions, which retain caller-supplied dates.

branchId.description: Deprecated: use `branchCode` instead. This field will be removed in a future major release. If both `branchId` and `branchCode` are provided, `branchCode` takes precedence.

fundsAvailabilitySchedule.description: Optional list of funds availability schedule tranches for this credit deposit. When present, the total amount withheld from the available balance equals the sum of all tranche amounts.

PendingTransactionSettleTransactions.description: One to ten posted transactions to book in place of the pending transaction. For a single-transaction settlement (most consumers) supply one entry; multi-transaction settlements (e.g., principal plus fee, multi-currency conversions, or fan-out distributions) supply additional entries. Each entry uses `SettlePendingTransactionPostedTransactionInput` and does not accept caller-supplied date fields — Core always books on the current system business date.

SettlePendingTransactionInput.description: Resolution input that settles the pending transaction by booking one or more posted transactions. The settle amount may differ from the pending amount (e.g., the final settlement of a debit-card authorization). Each entry in `transactions` is booked on the Posted Balance <<glossary:atomically>> with the release of the pending entry.

CancelPendingTransactionInput.description:
Resolution input that releases the pending transaction without settlement. The pending entry's contribution to the Pending Balance is removed; any associated funds-availability schedule is removed and the held funds are released.

The `transactions` field is forbidden for this resolution type. The polymorphism standard forbids `oneOf`/`anyOf`, so this prohibition is enforced by the server rather than expressed declaratively in the schema; a `CANCEL` request that includes a `transactions` array is rejected.

ResolutionType.title: Resolution Type
ResolutionType.description: The intent of a Resolve Pending Transaction request. `SETTLE` requires a `transactions` array describing the posted transaction(s) to book; `CANCEL` releases the pending entry without settlement and forbids the `transactions` field.

FundsAvailabilityUpdateReason.title: Funds Availability Update Reason
FundsAvailabilityUpdateReason.description: The auditable reason for replacing a deposit's currently-active funds availability schedule tranches. Required on every update for Regulation CC audit trails; the value is persisted on the ledger entries produced by the update.

x-enum-description.EXTENDED_HOLD_EXCEPTION_REVIEW: The schedule is being replaced following review of an extended hold placed under a Regulation CC exception (e.g. reasonable-cause or large-deposit exception hold).
x-enum-description.LARGE_DEPOSIT_RECONSIDERATION: The schedule is being replaced after reconsidering the availability applied to a large deposit above the Regulation CC threshold.
x-enum-description.DUPLICATE_DEPOSIT_CORRECTION: The schedule is being replaced to correct availability applied to a deposit that was identified as a duplicate.
x-enum-description.CUSTOMER_DISPUTE_RESOLUTION: The schedule is being replaced as a result of resolving a customer dispute relating to the deposit's availability.
x-enum-description.REGULATORY_REEVALUATION: The schedule is being replaced following a regulatory re-evaluation or re-disclosure of the deposit's funds availability.
x-enum-description.CLIENT_RISK_EVALUATION: The schedule is being replaced because the client's asynchronous risk evaluation of the deposit completed and the availability is being adjusted accordingly.

UpdateFundsAvailabilityScheduleInput.description: Input for replacing all currently-active funds availability tranches on a previously posted credit deposit with a new set, or clearing the schedule entirely via `unset` to release all held funds immediately. The update is atomic: all existing unreleased tranches are cancelled and the new schedule (or none, if `unset`) is applied in a single transaction. Exactly one of `fundsAvailabilitySchedule` or `unset` must be provided.

fundsAvailabilitySchedule.description: The new set of funds availability tranches that replaces all currently-active tranches. Every tranche must have an `availableFrom` strictly after the current UTC date-time. To release funds on specific tranches immediately, omit them from this array. Mutually exclusive with `unset`.

unset.description: When `true`, clears the entire active funds availability schedule instead of replacing it with a new one, releasing all held funds immediately. Mutually exclusive with `fundsAvailabilitySchedule`.

ScheduleReleaseBalances.description: Account balances captured immediately after a funds availability schedule operation. See Balances for information on balance types.

availableBalance.description: The amount of funds that are available for withdrawal after this operation was applied.

customerUncollected.description: The amount of funds that are not available for withdrawal because they are uncleared funds from a deposit, after this operation was applied.

UpdateFundsAvailabilityScheduleResult.description: Result of replacing a deposit's currently-active funds availability schedule tranches. Contains the new active schedule, the cancelled previous schedule, the timestamp at which the update took effect, and the resulting account balances.

updatedSchedule.description: The new set of active funds availability tranches created by this update. Each entry carries a server-assigned `scheduleId` that uniquely identifies the tranche. Empty when the update was an `unset`, releasing all held funds immediately.

previousSchedule.description: The set of funds availability tranches that were active before this update and have now been cancelled. Provided for caller confirmation and audit reconciliation.

updatedAt.description: The UTC date-time at which the schedule update took effect and the ledger entries were posted. Entries are always booked on the current business date.

resultingBalances.description: Account balances immediately after the update was applied, reflecting the net impact of removing the previous tranches and adding the new ones.

customerUncollectedNetBalance.description: The net change in the account's Customer Uncollected balance as a result of this update. A positive amount indicates held funds increased (more uncollected); a negative amount indicates held funds decreased (funds released to available).

holdBalance.description: The amount of funds that are not available for withdrawal because they are reserved for a specific purpose. Keep in mind that `holdBalance` could be greater than `ledgerBalance`, meaning that more funds are being held than exist in the account.

customerUncollected.description: The amount of funds that are not available for withdrawal because they are uncleared funds from a deposit. Keep in mind that `customerUncollected` could be greater than `ledgerBalance`, meaning that more funds are being held than exist in the account.

pendingBalance.description: The net signed contribution of unresolved pending transactions to the available balance. Pending debits reduce, and pending credits increase, this value. The Available Balance formula is `ledgerBalance + pendingBalance - customerUncollected - holdBalance`.

HoldStatus.title: HoldStatus
HoldStatus.description:
Specifies the hold status to retrieve:
- `VALID` — The hold is valid.
- `EXPIRED` — The hold has expired.
- `CANCELLED` — The hold was cancelled before expiration.

AccountHoldType.title: accountHoldType
AccountHoldType.description: Specifies the reason for placing a hold on account funds. - When creating a hold, set this value to the `holdType` that indicates the hold's purpose. - When retrieving holds, this field contains the `holdType` that was set when the hold was created. For standard hold types, see Holds and Hold Types. You may have additional custom values configured for your core. These values must consist of upper-case letters and underscores only, such as `CUSTOM_HOLD_TYPE`. If you attempt to pass a value that is not configured for your core, the endpoint will return an error.

ExternalAccountHoldId.description:
When creating a hold, use the `externalReferenceId` to specify a reference value from the calling system to provide a cross-reference between systems. This value may be used as the reference ID (together with the account) for subsequent inquiry and delete functions.

When retrieving holds, this is the `externalReferenceId` submitted when the hold was created.

When deleting a hold by external reference ID, this is the `externalReferenceId` submitted when the hold was created.

effectiveDate.description: The start date of the hold. If omitted, defaults to the current system date. If provided, the value must equal the current system date. A date before or after the current system date is rejected. Setting a future date for a hold to take effect is not supported.

expirationDate.description: The last date of the hold. The hold remains active until the system date advances to the next date or beyond `expirationDate`. **Example**: If the value is `2027-10-21` (Thursday), the hold is lifted when the system date advances to or beyond `2027-10-22`. For more information see System and Transaction Dates. **Format**: ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD). See Filter Ranges for more information on queries.

AccountHoldId.description: Hold ID created by the system to identify the hold for subsequent processes
AccountHoldId.title: holdId

holdId.description: The unique key for the hold record used to inquire on or delete the hold.

effectiveDate.description: The persisted start date of the hold.

AvailableBalanceOptions.description: Specifies the processing option related to available balance for this hold function to be successful. See Processing options for information about each option.

HoldUpdateBalances.description: Account balances affected by a hold update, captured immediately after the update was applied. See Balances for information on balance types.

holdBalance.description: Total of unsettled holds on the account after this operation. Pending transactions are not included.

availableBalance.description: The account available balance after this operation was applied.

resultingBalances.description: Account balances after the hold was created, captured immediately after the operation was applied.

HoldLookupId.title: HoldLookupId
HoldLookupId.description: An identifier used to look up a single hold — either an internal `holdId` or a caller-supplied `externalReferenceId`. The `idType` query parameter determines how this value is interpreted.

DeleteAccountHoldResult.description: Result of an accepted Delete Account Hold operation: the resulting account balances after the hold was released.

resultingBalances.description: Account balances after the hold was released, captured immediately after the operation was applied.

HoldAmountUpdate.description: The hold-amount change applied by an Update Account Hold request. The `updateMode` discriminator selects whether the current hold amount is fully replaced or suffers an adjustment. Both modes share the single underlying hold-amount movement: the server posts a debit to increase the hold and a credit to decrease it. `ABSOLUTE` derives the direction from `delta = holdAmount − currentHoldAmount`; `ADJUSTMENT` takes the direction directly from the explicit `adjustmentType`.

AbsoluteHoldAmountUpdate.description: Sets the hold to an absolute total amount. The server computes `delta = holdAmount − currentHoldAmount` under the account lock: a positive delta increases the hold, a negative delta decreases it, and a zero delta (with no expiration change) is rejected with `NO_OP_HOLD_UPDATE_REJECTED`. A negative `holdAmount` is rejected with `HOLD_AMOUNT_WOULD_GO_NEGATIVE`.

holdAmount.description: The new total hold amount. Must be non-negative and use the same currency as the account.

HoldAdjustmentType.title: Hold Adjustment Type
HoldAdjustmentType.description: Type of an ADJUSTMENT hold-amount update: INCREASE grows the hold (posted as a debit), DECREASE shrinks it (posted as a credit). Combine with the unsigned `adjustmentAmount` for the signed movement.

AdjustmentHoldAmountUpdate.description: Applies a directional delta to the current hold amount. `adjustmentType = INCREASE` grows the hold (posted as a debit); `adjustmentType = DECREASE` shrinks it (posted as a credit). A `DECREASE` that would drive the hold amount below zero is rejected with `HOLD_AMOUNT_WOULD_GO_NEGATIVE`, and a zero `adjustmentAmount` (with no expiration change) is rejected with `NO_OP_HOLD_UPDATE_REJECTED`.

adjustmentAmount.description: The unsigned magnitude to apply to the current hold amount; combine with `adjustmentType` for the signed movement. Must use the same currency as the account.

HoldUpdateMode.title: Hold Update Mode
HoldUpdateMode.description: How an Update Account Hold request expresses the change to the hold amount. `ABSOLUTE` sets the hold to a specific total (`holdAmount`); the server derives the movement direction from the difference against the current hold amount. `ADJUSTMENT` applies a signed delta (`adjustmentAmount`) to the current hold amount, where the sign gives the direction directly.

UpdateAccountHoldInput.description: Input for updating an existing hold's amount and/or expiration date. The optional `amountUpdate` object carries the hold-amount change and is omitted for an expiration-only update. The optional `requestorTimestamp` is the ordering anchor used to reject out-of-sequence (stale) updates. An update that does not change the hold amount and does not change the expiration is rejected as a no-op.

requestorTimestamp.description: Optional time the requesting system determined this update was needed. When supplied, it is used to order out-of-sequence updates: an incoming value older than the recorded anchor is rejected with `STALE_HOLD_UPDATE_REJECTED`; equal-or-later values are applied and become the new recorded anchor. When omitted, no staleness check is performed for this update, and the previously recorded anchor (if any) is left unchanged — a later update that does supply `requestorTimestamp` is still checked against it.

expirationDate.description: Optional new last date of the hold. When supplied, the hold's expiration is updated together with the amount change (or as the sole change for an expiration-only update). Format: ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD).

amountUpdate.description: Optional hold-amount change. Omit for an expiration-only update. When present, `updateMode` selects how the new amount is expressed.

UpdateAccountHoldResult.description: Result of an accepted Update Account Hold operation: the hold's resulting amount, the hold's resulting expiration date, and the resulting account balances.

externalReferenceId.description: The caller-supplied external reference for the hold, echoed back when one was recorded at creation. Omitted for holds created without an external reference.

expirationDate.description: The hold's expiration date after this update was applied, whether or not this update changed it. Omitted when the hold has no expiration date.

resultingHoldAmount.description: The hold amount after the update was applied.

resultingBalances.description: Account balances after the update was applied.

ResolveAccountHoldInput.description: Input for atomically updating the target hold's amount and/or expiration date while posting one or more transactions against the account in the same operation, succeeding or failing together. Both `holdUpdate` and `transactions` are required: a caller that only needs to post transactions without touching the hold should call `CreateDepositsAccountTransaction` instead.

holdUpdate.description: The hold-amount and/or expiration change, using the same semantics as `UpdateAccountHoldInput`. A `holdUpdate` that does not change the hold amount and does not change the expiration is rejected as a no-op (`NO_OP_HOLD_UPDATE_REJECTED`), regardless of `transactions`.

transactions.description: One to ten posted transactions to book atomically with the hold update.

ResolveAccountHoldBalances.description: Account balances captured immediately after a Resolve Account Hold operation was applied. Extends `TransactionBalances` (the same `resultingBalances` shape returned for posted transactions) with the account hold total, since a Resolve Account Hold operation posts transactions and updates a hold atomically. See Balances for information on balance types.

holdBalance.description: Total of unsettled holds on the account after this operation. Pending transactions are not included; their net contribution to the available balance is reported separately as `pendingBalance`.

ResolveAccountHoldResult.description: Result of an accepted Resolve Account Hold operation: the identifier of the resolved hold (`holdId`, plus the caller-supplied `externalReferenceId` when one was recorded), the hold's resulting amount, the hold's resulting expiration date, the identifiers of the transactions posted, and the resulting account balances — all committed atomically with the hold update.

externalReferenceId.description: The caller-supplied external reference for the hold, echoed back when one was recorded at creation. Omitted for holds created without an external reference.

expirationDate.description: The hold's expiration date after this update was applied, whether or not this update changed it. Omitted when the hold has no expiration date.

resultingHoldAmount.description: The hold amount after the operation was applied.

transactionIds.description: Unique identifiers for the transactions posted by this operation, in the same order as the `transactions` array in the request.

resultingBalances.description: Account balances after the operation was applied.

effectiveDate.description: The start date of the hold. If omitted, defaults to the current system date. If provided, the value must equal the current system date. A date before or after the current system date is rejected. Setting a future date for a hold to take effect is not supported.

expirationDate.description: The last date of the hold. The hold remains active until the system date advances to the next date or beyond `expirationDate`. **Example**: If the value is `2027-10-21` (Thursday), the hold is lifted when the system date advances to or beyond `2027-10-22`. For more information see System and Transaction Dates. **Format**: ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD). See Filter Ranges for more information on queries.

serialNumber.description: Typically a check number, this numeric value links the current transaction with a processing ticket. When this parameter is used with a `transactionCode` that indicates an actual check, this value is used for Stop Payment processing.

description.title: Description
description.description: Free-form field containing customer-facing notes. This field is not processed or protected and should therefore not contain any sensitive data.
examples: Bank-to-bank transfer from Criterion First National Bank

branchId.description: Deprecated: use `branchCode` instead. This field will be removed in a future major release. If both `branchId` and `branchCode` are provided, `branchCode` takes precedence.

actions.description: Defines the sequence of actions, in the order they are specified, to be executed atomically. See Using the Transact Account Action Endpoints for instructions.

TransactAccountResult.description: Indicates that an action succeeded. In the case of a partial success, further details are provided.

resultingBalances.description: Account balances after the hold was created, captured immediately after the operation was applied.

fundsAvailabilitySchedule.description: Schedule tranches created alongside this deposit. Present only when the request included a fundsAvailabilitySchedule array.

results.description:
The results of each action in the account transaction. This array will be the same length as
the requested `.actions`, with each result in the same position as its action request.

availableBalance.description: The amount of funds that are available for withdrawal. This is the `ledgerBalance` minus `holdsNonRegCCAmount`, `customerUncollectedAmount`.

holdsNonRegCCAmount.description: The sum of all active holds on the account that are NOT `holdType: FUNDS_AVAILABILITY`.

customerUncollectedAmount.description: The amount of funds that are not available for withdrawal because they are uncleared funds from a deposit. Keep in mind that `customerUncollectedAmount` could be greater than `ledgerBalance`, meaning that more funds are being held than exist in the account.

debitCardOptInAmount.description: The allowed overdraft amount for the account when performing a debit card purchase or debit transaction, and the account has opted in to Debit Card Courtesy Approval.

debitCardOptInBalance.description: The amount of funds that may be withdrawn from the account when performing a debit card purchase or debit transaction, and the account has opted in to Debit Card Courtesy Approval.

customerCollected.description: The amount of funds that is not subject to withdrawal restrictions due to uncollected funds as part of a credit to the account.

customerUncollectedOneBusinessDay.description: The sum of all active holds on the account where `holdType: FUNDS_AVAILABILITY` and the hold expiration date is equal to the current business date.

customerUncollectedTwoBusinessDay.description: The sum of all active holds on the account where `holdType: FUNDS_AVAILABILITY` and the hold expiration date is equal to the current business date + 1 business day.

customerUncollectedThreeBusinessDay.description: The sum of all active holds on the account where `holdType: FUNDS_AVAILABILITY` and the hold expiration date is equal to the current business date + 2 business days.

customerUncollectedFourBusinessDay.description: The sum of all active holds on the account where `holdType: FUNDS_AVAILABILITY` and the hold expiration date is equal to the current business date + 3 business days.

customerUncollectedFiveBusinessDay.description: The sum of all active holds on the account where `holdType: FUNDS_AVAILABILITY` and the hold expiration date is equal to the current business date + 4 business days.

customerUncollectedSixBusinessDay.description: The sum of all active holds on the account where `holdType: FUNDS_AVAILABILITY` and the hold expiration date is equal to the current business date + 5 business days.

customerUncollectedSevenBusinessDay.description: The sum of all active holds on the account where `holdType: FUNDS_AVAILABILITY` and the hold expiration date is equal to the current business date + 6 or more business days.

bankCollected.description: The amount of funds held in the account which has been cleared through the exchange process between banks.  This amount would be used to calculate interest when the financial institution pays interest only on cleared funds rather than the ledger balance (all funds in the account).

bankUncollectedOneBusinessDay.description: The amount of funds that are considered `bankUncollected` but will no longer be uncollected on the current business date + 1 business day.

bankUncollectedTwoBusinessDay.description: The amount of funds that are considered `bankUncollected` but will no longer be uncollected on the current business date + 2 business days.

bankUncollectedThreeBusinessDay.description: The amount of funds that are considered `bankUncollected` but will no longer be uncollected on the current business date + 3 business days.

bankUncollectedFourBusinessDay.description: The amount of funds that are considered `bankUncollected` but will no longer be uncollected on the current business date + 4 business days.

bankUncollectedFiveBusinessDay.description: The amount of funds that are considered `bankUncollected` but will no longer be uncollected on the current business date + 5 business days.

bankUncollectedSixBusinessDay.description: The amount of funds that are considered `bankUncollected` but will no longer be uncollected on the current business date + 6 business days.

bankUncollectedSevenBusinessDay.description: The amount of funds that are considered `bankUncollected` but will no longer be uncollected on the current business date + 7 business days.

UpdateAccountSettingsInput.description: Populate the `settings` object with values to apply, or populate the `unset` object to remove  one or more settings, or you can populate both in the same request as long as a setting key does not appear in both `settings` and `unset` simultaneously. You must pass a value in at least one object or the request will be rejected.

unset.description: Array of setting keys to explicitly remove/disable.

AccountClosed.description:
This schema defines the structure of an account closure event.
It includes details about the account closing action, such as the reason for closure, the closeout amount, and applicable withholding amounts.

productAndSubProduct.description: Deprecated: use `productCode` instead. This object will be removed in a future major release.

closeDate.title: Closing Date
closeDate.description: The date on which the account was officially closed.

closeoutAmount.description: The total amount required to settle the account and bring the ledger balance to zero.

closeoutInterestPaid.description: The gross interest paid on this close, before withholding, based on the prior day's interest balance and the same rounding the close applied. This is the `closeoutInterestPaid` component of the closeout formula (`closeoutAmount = ledgerBalance + closeoutInterestPaid - sum(closeoutTaxWithholding by code)`). Non-negative; omitted when no interest was paid on this close.

closeoutTaxWithholding.title: Closeout Tax Withholding by Code
closeoutTaxWithholding.description: Tax withheld from the interest paid on this close, broken out by withholding code. One entry per code that applied; codes that did not apply are omitted, and a reported zero means the code applied with a zero amount. The sum of these amounts is the withholding term of the closeout formula (`closeoutAmount = ledgerBalance + closeoutInterestPaid - sum(closeoutTaxWithholding by code)`). An empty array means no withholding applied.

accruedInterestAmount.description: Deprecated: replaced by `closeoutInterestPaid`. This field reported the gross interest earned on the account balance; consumers should read `closeoutInterestPaid` instead. It will be removed in a future major release.

federalWithholdingAmount.description: Deprecated: replaced by the per-code `closeoutTaxWithholding` breakdown, which does not require federal/state classification. This field reported the portion of the interest withheld as federal income tax; consumers should read `closeoutTaxWithholding` instead. It will be removed in a future major release.

stateWithholdingAmount.description: Deprecated: replaced by the per-code `closeoutTaxWithholding` breakdown, which does not require federal/state classification. This field reported the portion of the interest withheld as state income tax; consumers should read `closeoutTaxWithholding` instead. It will be removed in a future major release.

branchId.description: Deprecated: use `branchCode` instead. This field will be removed in a future major release.

AccountCreated.description: This schema defines the structure of an account creation event.

AccountUpdated.description: This schema defines the structure of an account update event.

ExecutionUniqueId.title: ExecutionUniqueId
ExecutionUniqueId.description: Execution unique id by job instance

EodStatus.title: EodStatus
EodStatus.description: The status of the end of day execution, such as `SUCCESS`, `FAILED`. `SUCCESS`: The end of day execute all jobs successfully. `FAILED`: The end of day execute but any job generate an error.

DepositsEoDEnd.description:
This is a **draft schema** for the `EoD End` event, intended for initial development and CI/CD integration purposes.
It represents the basic structure of an event emitted when a new eod execution is finish in the system. The schema includes
essential fields such as execution unique ID, business date, jobName, and timestamp. This provisional definition enables progress on
event handling and artifact publication while the final schema is being reviewed and refined.

DepositsEoDStart.description:
This is a **draft schema** for the `EoD Start` event, intended for initial development and CI/CD integration purposes.
It represents the basic structure of an event emitted when a new eod execution is started in the system. The schema includes
essential fields such as execution unique ID, business date, jobName, and timestamp. This provisional definition enables progress on
event handling and artifact publication while the final schema is being reviewed and refined.

FundsAvailabilityScheduleCreated.description:
Event emitted when a funds availability schedule is created alongside a credit deposit transaction.
One event is emitted per deposit transaction that includes a fundsAvailabilitySchedule payload.
Each item in the schedule array represents one tranche with its specific release date and amount.

fundsAvailabilitySchedule.description: The list of schedule tranches created for this deposit. At least one item is always present.

resultingBalances.description: The account's resulting available balance after this deposit and its funds availability schedule were posted, captured immediately after the operation was applied.

FundsAvailabilityScheduleReleased.description:
Event emitted when a single funds-availability tranche is released — its uncollected hold
expires and the funds become available. One event is emitted per tranche at the moment the
tranche's release deadline fires (validUntil reached) and the release ledger transaction is
posted. scheduleId matches the scheduleId of the corresponding tranche in the
FundsAvailabilityScheduleCreated event, providing reconciliation linkage.

transactionId.description: Identifier of the release ledger transaction that made the tranche available.

originatingTransactionId.description: Identifier of the originating deposit ledger transaction that created this tranche.

expirationDate.description: The date-time at which this tranche became available (the tranche validUntil / availableFrom). Echoes the availableFrom of the corresponding created tranche.

regulationCCObligation.description: Whether the originating tranche was subject to Regulation CC obligations. Sourced from the originating CUSTOMER_UNCOLLECTED entry's funds-availability metadata.

resultingBalances.description: Account balances affected by this schedule release, captured immediately after the funds were released.

FundsAvailabilityScheduleUpdated.description:
Event emitted when a deposit's currently-active funds-availability schedule is replaced via the
Update Funds Availability Schedule operation. A single event is emitted per accepted update, in
the same database transaction as the ledger writes (transactional outbox), carrying the schedule
state before and after the update, the auditable update reason, and the resulting account balances.

The event drives downstream Regulation CC customer-notification. Regulation CC indicator changes
are conveyed by comparing the `regulationCCObligation` flag on each tranche between
`previousSchedule` and `updatedSchedule` (a tranche's flag may differ from the original).

`updatedSchedule` is the new active tranche set; `previousSchedule` is the set that was active
before the update and has now been cancelled. `scheduleId` on each entry provides reconciliation
linkage to the FundsAvailabilityScheduleCreated / FundsAvailabilityScheduleReleased events.

transactionId.description: Identifier of the originating deposit ledger transaction whose funds-availability schedule was updated.

updatedSchedule.description: The new set of active funds-availability tranches created by this update. Each entry carries a server-assigned `scheduleId`. Compare `regulationCCObligation` against `previousSchedule` to detect Regulation CC indicator changes. Empty when the update was an `unset`, releasing all held funds immediately.

previousSchedule.description: The set of funds-availability tranches that were active before this update and have now been cancelled. Provided for audit reconciliation and Regulation CC change detection.

updatedAt.description: The UTC date-time at which the schedule update took effect and the ledger entries were posted. Mirrors `updatedAt` on the UpdateFundsAvailabilitySchedule operation response.

resultingBalances.description: Account balances captured immediately after the update was applied, reflecting the net impact of removing the previous tranches and adding the new ones.

customerUncollectedNetBalance.description: The net change in the account's Customer Uncollected balance as a result of this update. A positive amount indicates held funds increased (more uncollected); a negative amount indicates held funds decreased (funds released to available).

HoldCreated.description:
This schema defines the structure of a hold creation event in the core deposits system.
It is emitted when a hold is successfully created on an account.

resultingBalances.description: Account balances after the hold was created, captured immediately after the operation was applied.

effectiveDate.description: The start date of the hold. Equals the system date at creation.

HoldDeleted.description:
This schema defines the structure of a hold deletion event in the core deposits system.
It is emitted when a hold on an account is either manually cancelled or has expired.

resultingBalances.description: Account balances after the hold was released or expired, captured immediately after the operation was applied.

effectiveDate.description: The start date of the hold.

PendingTransactionCreated.description:
Emitted when a pending transaction is successfully recorded in the ledger. The event is
persisted to the outbox in the same database transaction as the ledger entry, guaranteeing
exactly-once delivery under the transactional outbox pattern. Downstream consumers (fraud
screening, notifications, analytics) use this event to react to newly created pending
entries without polling the API.

status.description: Always `PENDING` for this event type. Included so that consumers can use a single envelope for both created and resolved pending-transaction events.

branchId.description: Deprecated: use `branchCode` instead. This field will be removed in a future major release.

productAndSubProduct.description: Deprecated: use `productCode` instead. This object will be removed in a future major release.

PendingTransactionDeclined.description:
Emitted when a pending transaction creation is rejected with a whitelisted business error.
The event is persisted to the outbox in a separate database transaction from the rejected
attempt (via `REQUIRES_NEW` propagation), so the rejection itself is never persisted to
the ledger while the event survives for downstream observability.

Only a curated set of `ServiceError` codes trigger this event — validation errors such as
malformed input or unknown transaction codes, and not-found errors, do **not** produce a
declined event.

branchId.description: Deprecated: use `branchCode` instead. This field will be removed in a future major release.

productAndSubProduct.description: Deprecated: use `productCode` instead. This object will be removed in a future major release.

PendingTransactionResolved.description:
Emitted when a pending transaction is resolved — either settled by booking one or more
posted transactions (`resolution.outcome: POSTED`) or released without settlement
(`resolution.outcome: CANCELLED`). The event payload mirrors the `ResolvePendingTransaction`
endpoint response (`PendingTransaction` with `status: RESOLVED`) so consumers receive the
same view of the entry whether they observe it via API response or event stream.

The event is persisted to the outbox in the same database transaction as the resolution
itself, guaranteeing exactly-once delivery under the transactional outbox pattern.

branchId.description: Deprecated: use `branchCode` instead. This field will be removed in a future major release.

productAndSubProduct.description: Deprecated: use `productCode` instead. This object will be removed in a future major release.

direction.description: Accounting direction (DEBIT or CREDIT) of this pending transaction, derived from the transaction code's catalog entry.

timestamp.description: The exact time when the pending transaction was originally recorded. Format: RFC 3339 (ISO 8601) YYYY-MM-DD`T`hh:mm:ss.sss`Z`.

resultingBalances.description: Balance dimensions captured immediately after the pending entry was resolved.

fundsAvailabilitySchedule.description: Funds-availability schedule tranches declared on the original pending transaction. Released on `CANCELLED`; not carried over to posted transaction(s) on `POSTED`.

PendingTransactionSupersedeRejected.description:
Emitted when a `:supersede` call is rejected due to direction/netting validation failure —
specifically when the `transactions` and `successor` carry an inconsistent accounting direction
or sign relative to the original pending transaction.

The event is persisted to the outbox in a separate database transaction from the rejected
attempt (via `REQUIRES_NEW` propagation), so the rejection itself is never written to the
ledger while the event survives for downstream observability.

Only the `DIRECTION_MISMATCH` rejection scenario triggers this event. All other `:supersede`
failure modes (e.g. insufficient balance, already-resolved) remain silent.

pendingTransactionId.description: Internal identifier of the original pending transaction (P1) whose `:supersede` was rejected.

rejectionReason.description: Machine-readable reason code explaining why the `:supersede` was rejected.

productAndSubProduct.description: Deprecated: use `productCode` instead. This object will be removed in a future major release.

timestamp.description: The exact time when the rejection occurred. Format: RFC 3339 (ISO 8601) YYYY-MM-DD`T`hh:mm:ss.sss`Z`.
